resources.string: Shown while the phone is connected to a car display.
Finds out what your car checks about the phone\'s certificate. Each connection presents a different identity and records how far it got and why it stopped.
Plug the phone into the car
The car accepted a certificate we generated
The car has not spoken yet
Start the engine and let the car screen finish booting.
Plug the phone into the car\'s data USB port, with a good cable.
Leave it connected for a minute. A car that refuses usually retries by itself, and each retry advances the probe.
Unplug and plug back in until every identity has been tried, then share the report.
What the car presented to us
No public source records this for this model of head unit. Its issuer identifies who actually built the projection software in these cars.
This car does not require a certificate issued by Google. Nobody has published that result before — it is worth reporting.
Every identity was refused during the handshake. The alert on each row names the check that failed. This is the expected outcome, and it is the first published measurement of it.
The handshake succeeded and the car refused afterwards. It accepted the certificate as a certificate and rejected the identity, which is a more specific finding than a chain failure.
The car never spoke. That is a cable, port or connection problem rather than a verdict about certificates. Try another cable, and check the car has Android Auto enabled.
